ordered_diagnoses: Pulmonary Atresia with Intact Ventricular Septum

candidates.name: Tricuspid Atresia
support_spans: severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice
candidates.why: The presence of a hypoplastic left ventricle and reduced mitral valve orifice suggests tricuspid atresia.

candidates.name: Pulmonary Atresia with Intact Ventricular Septum
support_spans: severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle
contradict_spans: a 6 mm muscular interventricular defect in the dorsal septum
candidates.why: The presence of two great vessels arising from the right ventricle and severe right-sided dilation suggests pulmonary atresia, but the intact ventricular septum is contradicted by the presence of an interventricular defect.

candidates.name: Ebstein's Anomaly
support_spans: severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
severe tricuspid regurgitation
contradict_spans: a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice
candidates.why: The presence of severe tricuspid regurgitation and right-sided dilation suggests Ebstein's anomaly, but the hypoplastic left ventricle is not typical of this condition.

key_evidence_spans: severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice
two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle

candidates.name: Tricuspid Atresia
support_spans: severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice
contradict_spans: a 16 mm interatrial defect in the upper septum
candidates.why: The presence of severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, along with a hypoplastic left ventricle, suggests a condition where blood flow is restricted to the left side of the heart.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be overlooked due to the complexity of the cardiac defects and the presence of multiple septal defects.

candidates.name: Pulmonary Atresia with Intact Ventricular Septum
support_spans: severe tricuspid regurgitation
two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle
contradict_spans: a 6 mm muscular interventricular defect in the dorsal septum
candidates.why: The combination of severe tricuspid regurgitation and the presence of two great vessels arising from the right ventricle suggests a condition where the pulmonary valve is atretic.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be challenging to identify due to the presence of multiple cardiac defects and the need for detailed imaging studies.

candidates.name: Double Outlet Right Ventricle
support_spans: two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle
severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
contradict_spans: a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice
candidates.why: The presence of two great vessels arising from the right ventricle, along with severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, suggests a condition where both great vessels originate from the right ventricle.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be overlooked due to the complexity of the cardiac defects and the need for detailed imaging studies.
